mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes earnings downgrades and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases uncertainty and reduces S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between monthly HOUST (housing starts) and GDPC1 signals robust residential investment and broad-based demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 positively correlated (> 0.6) in last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO above its 6-month moving average, combined with a stable RSAFS (retail sales), signals improving supply capacity without overheating demand, which supports moderate and stable S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 6-month MA for 3 consecutive months and RSAFS stable (|monthly change| < 0.5%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered windows.
